claims.text: Partially substituting Mn in a Ni-Mn-based Heusler alloy with a rare-earth element such as Tb will alter its magnetic interactions.
Rare-earth substitution for Mn will alter the alloy's phase-transition behavior.
Rare-earth substitution for Mn will enhance the alloy's magnetocaloric properties near room temperature.
The undoped Ni-Mn-based Heusler alloy exhibits a magnetocaloric effect near room temperature.
Tb incorporation changes the magnetic exchange interactions in the alloy.
Tb incorporation changes the electronic structure of the alloy.
Changes in magnetic exchange interactions and electronic structure modify magnetic ordering.
The dopant modifies the balance of magnetic interactions.
Modification of magnetic interactions broadens or shifts the magnetic transition.
Broadening or shifting the magnetic transition increases the adiabatic temperature change.
Broadening or shifting the magnetic transition increases the isothermal entropy change.
Tb-doped material will exhibit a statistically significant increase in adiabatic temperature change relative to the undoped alloy.
Tb-doped material will exhibit a statistically significant increase in isothermal entropy change relative to the undoped alloy.
Tb doping will broaden the useful magnetocaloric operating-temperature range relative to the undoped alloy.
